answer: The most convincing defense is vested payouts: every reward an agent earns is locked and released in small slices over many future epochs, so its income arrives as a slow crystal of value rather than cash. A sybil farmer must whisper the same promise across thousands of identities, but each fake account forfeits unvested earnings the moment it is slashed or goes silent. The copper cost of running a vast bot swarm then exceeds anything the vesting tail ever pays out, so flash-farming collapses under its own burn rate.
